lemmas.proof_markdown:
The table has $p^2(p+1)\epsilon$ accepted incidences. Double counting them by their point and line endpoints gives

$$\sum_x a_x=p^2(p+1)\epsilon,\qquad \sum_L b_L=p^2(p+1)\epsilon.$$

Since there are $p^2$ points and $p(p+1)$ affine lines,

$$\mathbb E_x[a_x]=(p+1)\epsilon,\qquad \mathbb E_L[b_L]=p\epsilon.$$

Condition on a point $x$. Among the $(p+1)_s$ ordered tuples of $s$ distinct lines through $x$, exactly $(a_x)_s$ consist entirely of accepted incidences. Averaging over $x$ proves the point identity. Likewise, conditioned on a line $L$, exactly $(b_L)_s$ of the $(p)_s$ ordered tuples of $s$ distinct points on $L$ are entirely accepted. Averaging over $L$ proves the line identity. The convention $(u)_0=1$ gives both identities at $s=0$. No independence or concentration estimate is used.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let a valid affine line-versus-point table over $\mathbb F_p^2$ have agreement $\epsilon$, accepted point degrees $a_x$, and accepted line degrees $b_L$. For integers $u,s\ge0$, write $(u)_0=1$ and, for $s\ge1$, $(u)_s=u(u-1)\cdots(u-s+1)$. For $0\le s\le p+1$, let $\Gamma_s^P$ be the probability that, after choosing a uniform point and an ordered $s$-tuple of distinct incident lines uniformly, all sampled incidences are accepted. For $0\le s\le p$, define $\Gamma_s^L$ analogously using a uniform line and an ordered $s$-tuple of distinct points on it. Then

$$\Gamma_s^P=\frac{\mathbb E_x[(a_x)_s]}{(p+1)_s}\qquad(0\le s\le p+1),$$

and

$$\Gamma_s^L=\frac{\mathbb E_L[(b_L)_s]}{(p)_s}\qquad(0\le s\le p).$$
lemmas.title: Distinct-star counts

lemmas.proof_markdown:
For $F_s(j)=(j)_s$, the forward differences satisfy

$$\Delta F_s(j)=s(j)_{s-1}$$

and, for $s\ge2$,

$$\Delta^2F_s(j)=s(s-1)(j)_{s-2}\ge0.$$

For $s=0$ and $s=1$, the function is respectively constant and affine. Thus the piecewise-linear interpolation of $j\mapsto(j)_s$ is convex. Jensen's inequality for any integer-valued degree variable $A$ gives

$$\mathbb E[(A)_s]\ge J_s(\mathbb E[A]).$$

The minimizer need not be unique when the falling factorial vanishes, but the adjacent-integer mixture always attains the minimum. Applying this inequality to $A=a_x$ and $A=b_L$, using the two mean identities from P1, proves the distinct-star bounds.

For sampling with replacement, conditioning on the center gives

$$\widetilde\Gamma_r^P=\mathbb E_x\left[\left(\frac{a_x}{p+1}\right)^r\right],\qquad \widetilde\Gamma_r^L=\mathbb E_L\left[\left(\frac{b_L}{p}\right)^r\right].$$

Ordinary Jensen applied to $z\mapsto z^r$ gives both lower bounds. Repeated samples must not be confused with distinct constraints: if $S(r,j)$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind, then

$$a^r=\sum_{j=0}^r S(r,j)(a)_j,$$

so the repeated-sampling moments include events in which sampled lines or points coincide.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let a valid affine line-versus-point table over $\mathbb F_p^2$ have agreement $\epsilon$. For every real $\mu\ge0$, put $k=\lfloor\mu\rfloor$ and $\rho=\mu-k$, and define

$$J_s(\mu)=(1-\rho)(k)_s+\rho(k+1)_s.$$

For every integer $r\ge1$, let $\widetilde\Gamma_r^P$ and $\widetilde\Gamma_r^L$ be the analogous all-accepted probabilities when the incident lines or points are sampled independently with replacement. Then

$$\Gamma_s^P\ge\frac{J_s((p+1)\epsilon)}{(p+1)_s}\qquad(0\le s\le p+1),$$

$$\Gamma_s^L\ge\frac{J_s(p\epsilon)}{(p)_s}\qquad(0\le s\le p),$$

and

$$\widetilde\Gamma_r^P\ge\epsilon^r,\qquad \widetilde\Gamma_r^L\ge\epsilon^r\qquad(r\ge1).$$
lemmas.title: Degree-moment envelopes

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Because $d<p$, the elements of $S_d$ are distinct in $\mathbb F_p$, and every displayed label is a monic polynomial of formal degree exactly $d<p$ with $d$ distinct roots.

On a nonvertical line $L_{m,b}$, an incidence with parameter $t$ is accepted exactly when

$$t+m\in S_d.$$

The accepted parameters are the $d$ distinct elements $t=s-m$, with $s\in S_d$. On a vertical line, the accepted parameters are exactly the $d$ elements of $S_d$. Hence $b_L=d$ for every affine line.

At a point $(x,y)$, a nonvertical line of slope $m$ accepts exactly when $x+m\in S_d$. For every $s\in S_d$, there is one such slope, namely $m=s-x$, so every point lies on exactly $d$ accepted nonvertical lines. Its vertical line accepts precisely when $y\in S_d$. Thus $a_{(x,y)}=d+1$ when $y\in S_d$ and $a_{(x,y)}=d$ otherwise. There are $p|S_d|=pd$ points of the first kind and $p(p-d)$ of the second.

Finally, the accepted graph has $dp(p+1)$ edges out of $p^2(p+1)$ incidences, so

$$\epsilon_0=\frac{dp(p+1)}{p^2(p+1)}=\frac dp.$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime and let $101\le d<p$. Define

$$S_d=\{0,1,\ldots,d-1\}\subset\mathbb F_p,\qquad f(x,y)=0.$$

For every $m,b\in\mathbb F_p$, parameterize the nonvertical line $L_{m,b}$ by $L_{m,b}(t)=(t,mt+b)$ and assign it the label

$$P_{m,b}(t)=\prod_{s\in S_d}(t+m-s).$$

For every $c\in\mathbb F_p$, parameterize the vertical line $V_c$ by $V_c(t)=(c,t)$ and assign it the label

$$P_{V_c}(t)=\prod_{s\in S_d}(t-s).$$

These data form a valid affine line-versus-point table of agreement $\epsilon_0=d/p$. Every label has formal degree exactly $d$, every affine line has accepted degree $d$, exactly $pd$ points have accepted degree $d+1$, and the remaining $p(p-d)$ points have accepted degree $d$.
lemmas.title: Affine carrier

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The elements $0$, $1$, and $2$ belong to $S_d$. Fix $(x,y)\in\mathbb F_p^2$ and put

$$C=(x-1,y+x-1).$$

The points $(x,y)$ and $C$ lie on a line of slope $1-x$. Their acceptance values are respectively

$$x+(1-x)=1\qquad\text{and}\qquad (x-1)+(1-x)=0,$$

so both incidences are accepted. The points $C$ and $(x,y+1)$ lie on a line of slope $2-x$, where their acceptance values are respectively

$$(x-1)+(2-x)=1\qquad\text{and}\qquad x+(2-x)=2.$$

Thus $(x,y)$ and $(x,y+1)$ are joined by a four-edge accepted path through $C$ and the two intervening line vertices.

The points $(x,y)$ and $(x+1,y-x)$ lie on the line of slope $-x$, and their acceptance values are $0$ and $1$. Hence an accepted two-edge path joins these points. Repeated vertical unit moves connect every point in a fixed column, and the second move connects column $x$ to column $x+1$. Since $1$ generates the additive group of the prime field $\mathbb F_p$, every point vertex lies in one component. Every affine line has $d>0$ accepted neighbors by P3, so every line vertex lies in the same component. P3 also gives positive degree at every point.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let the valid table be the table defined in P3. Its accepted bipartite point-line graph is connected, and every point of $\mathbb F_p^2$ and every affine line is a nonisolated vertex.
lemmas.title: Carrier graph

lemmas.proof_markdown:
By P3, the point degree is $d+1$ with probability $d/p=\epsilon_0$ and is $d$ with probability $1-d/p$. Its mean is

$$(p+1)\epsilon_0=d+\frac dp,$$

whose adjacent-integer mixture is precisely this distribution. Every line degree is constantly $p\epsilon_0=d$. Substitution into P1 gives the two exact moment formulas, and P2 shows that they attain both adjacent-integer lower envelopes for every admissible order. Constant line degree also gives

$$\widetilde\Gamma_r^L=\mathbb E_L\left[\left(\frac{b_L}{p}\right)^r\right]=\left(\frac dp\right)^r=\epsilon_0^r.$$

The falling factorial $(d)_s$ vanishes for $s>d$, and both $(d)_s$ and $(d+1)_s$ vanish for $s>d+1$. Consequently,

$$\Gamma_s^L=0\quad(d<s\le p),\qquad \Gamma_s^P=0\quad(d+1<s\le p+1).$$

Fixed mean alone cannot manufacture more distinct algebraic constraints than the local degree permits. Setting $s=2$ in the point formula gives

$$\Gamma_2^P=\epsilon_0^2-\frac{\epsilon_0(1-\epsilon_0)}{p+1}.$$

Moreover,

$$\frac{(d)_s}{(p)_s}=\prod_{i=0}^{s-1}\frac{d-i}{p-i}.$$

Every factor is at most $d/p=\epsilon_0$. If $2\le s\le(d+1)/2$, then for $1\le i\le s-1$ each corresponding factor is at least $\epsilon_0/2$, while the factor with $i=0$ equals $\epsilon_0$. Hence

$$2^{-(s-1)}\epsilon_0^s\le\frac{(d)_s}{(p)_s}\le\epsilon_0^s.$$

The exact falling-factorial ratio, rather than this coarse comparison, is retained in the conclusion.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let the table defined in P3 have agreement $\epsilon_0=d/p$. Then

$$\Gamma_s^P=\frac{(1-d/p)(d)_s+(d/p)(d+1)_s}{(p+1)_s}=\frac{J_s((p+1)\epsilon_0)}{(p+1)_s}\qquad(0\le s\le p+1),$$

$$\Gamma_s^L=\frac{(d)_s}{(p)_s}=\frac{J_s(p\epsilon_0)}{(p)_s}\qquad(0\le s\le p),$$

and, for every integer $r\ge1$,

$$\widetilde\Gamma_r^L=\epsilon_0^r.$$
lemmas.title: Carrier moments

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Replacing every weight $\lambda_M>1$ by $1$ does not change any capped load and cannot increase the objective. Thus the feasible weights may be restricted to the compact cube $[0,1]^{p(p+1)}$; the feasibility inequalities are closed, so the optimum is attained.

For any feasible $\lambda$, define

$$v_x=\min\left\{1,\sum_{M\ni x:(x,M)\in E}\lambda_M\right\}.$$

Since $u_{x,L}(\lambda)\le v_x$, P3 and double counting give

$$\theta d\,p(p+1)\le\sum_L\sum_{x:(x,L)\in E}u_{x,L}(\lambda)\le\sum_x a_xv_x\le(d+1)\sum_xv_x.$$

Moreover,

$$\sum_xv_x\le\sum_x\sum_{M\ni x:(x,M)\in E}\lambda_M=\sum_M b_M\lambda_M=d\sum_M\lambda_M.$$

Combining these inequalities yields

$$\theta d\,p(p+1)\le d(d+1)\sum_M\lambda_M,$$

which proves the lower bound.

For the upper bound, give every affine line the uniform real weight

$$\lambda_M=\frac{\theta}{d-1}.$$

At an accepted incidence $(x,L)$, there are at least $a_x-1\ge d-1$ other accepted lines through $x$. Their total weight is at least $\theta$, and $\theta\le1$, so $u_{x,L}(\lambda)\ge\theta$. These weights are $\theta$-reaching and have total weight $\theta p(p+1)/(d-1)$.

The ratio of the upper bound to the lower bound is

$$\frac{d+1}{d-1}\le\frac{102}{100}.$$

Since $d=p\epsilon_0$, the exact bounds give

$$\operatorname{OPT}_\theta=\Theta\left(\frac{\theta p}{\epsilon_0}\right).$$

The division by $d-1$ occurs in the real weight space and is valid because $d\ge101$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let the table defined in P3 have accepted edge set $E$ and agreement $\epsilon_0=d/p$. For nonnegative real line weights $\lambda=(\lambda_M)$, define

$$u_{x,L}(\lambda)=\min\left\{1,\sum_{\substack{M\ni x,\ M\ne L\\(x,M)\in E}}\lambda_M\right\}.$$

For $0<\theta\le1$, call $\lambda$ $\theta$-reaching if

$$\sum_{x:(x,L)\in E}u_{x,L}(\lambda)\ge\theta d$$

for every affine line $L$, and let $\operatorname{OPT}_\theta$ be the minimum of $\sum_M\lambda_M$ over all such weights. Then

$$\frac{\theta p(p+1)}{d+1}\le\operatorname{OPT}_\theta\le\frac{\theta p(p+1)}{d-1}.$$
lemmas.title: Fractional reaching

lemmas.proof_markdown:
In the affine plane, two distinct points determine exactly one affine line, and two distinct affine lines meet in at most one point. Thus the full point-line incidence graph has the asserted common-neighborhood property, and passing to an accepted subgraph cannot increase a common neighborhood. In particular, $G$ is $K_{2,2}$-free.

In a with-replacement dependent-random-choice sample, deduplicate the sampled vertices. If only one distinct vertex remains, its common neighborhood is a one-vertex star; if at least two distinct vertices remain, the common neighborhood has size at most $1$. This conclusion concerns only the raw point-line graph. The auxiliary compatibility graph $H$ may contain many four-cycles.
lemmas.statement_markdown: Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let $G$ be the bipartite accepted-incidence graph of a valid affine line-versus-point table over $\mathbb F_p^2$. Then $G$ contains no $K_{2,2}$, and every set of at least two distinct vertices on either shore of $G$ has at most one common neighbor.
lemmas.title: Affine incidence neighborhoods

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Every unordered pair of accepted lines through $x$ gives one edge of $H$, and every edge of $H$ has a unique intersection point. Hence

$$e(H)=\sum_x\binom{a_x}{2}.$$

Since the mean of $a_x$ is $\mu$ and $N=p(p+1)$,

$$\bar\Delta=\frac{2e(H)}N=\frac{p\,\mathbb E_x[a_x(a_x-1)]}{p+1}.$$

Convexity gives $\mathbb E_x[a_x(a_x-1)]\ge\mu(\mu-1)$, proving the stated bound. Because the degrees are integral, the adjacent-integer bound from P2 also gives the sharper form

$$\bar\Delta\ge\frac{pJ_2(\mu)}{p+1}.$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let a valid affine line-versus-point table over $\mathbb F_p^2$ have local agreement $\epsilon$. For each point $x$, let $a_x$ be its accepted-line degree, put $\mu=(p+1)\epsilon$ and $N=p(p+1)$, and let $H$ be the graph on the $N$ affine lines in which two distinct nonparallel lines are adjacent exactly when both accept their unique intersection. If $\bar\Delta=2e(H)/N$, then

$$e(H)=\sum_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}\binom{a_x}{2}$$

and

$$\bar\Delta\ge\frac{p\mu(\mu-1)}{p+1}.$$
lemmas.title: Compatibility graph degrees

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Count pairs $(S,L)$ in which $S$ is a $t$-element subset of $N_H(L)$. Their number is

$$\sum_L\binom{\deg_H(L)}t.$$

Averaging over the $\binom Nt$ possible sets $S$ gives one set of distinct seed lines with at least $M_t(H)$ common neighbors. Discrete convexity of $j\mapsto\binom jt$ gives

$$M_t(H)\ge N\frac{\binom{\lfloor\bar\Delta\rfloor}t}{\binom Nt}.$$

If $\bar\Delta\ge2t+2$, every numerator factor in the binomial ratio is at least $\bar\Delta/2$, while every denominator factor is at most $N$. Hence the ratio is at least $(\bar\Delta/(2N))^t$. By P8 and $\mu\ge2$,

$$\frac{\bar\Delta}{2N}\ge\frac{\mu(\mu-1)}{2(p+1)^2}\ge\frac{\epsilon^2}{4},$$

which proves the simplified bound.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P8, let $t$ be an integer with $1\le t\le\lfloor\bar\Delta\rfloor$, and define

$$M_t(H)=\frac{\sum_{L\in V(H)}\binom{\deg_H(L)}t}{\binom Nt}.$$

There is a set $S\subseteq V(H)$ of $t$ distinct lines such that

$$\left|\bigcap_{M\in S}N_H(M)\right|\ge M_t(H)\ge N\frac{\binom{\lfloor\bar\Delta\rfloor}t}{\binom Nt}.$$

If additionally $\mu\ge2$ and $\bar\Delta\ge2t+2$, then

$$M_t(H)\ge N\left(\frac{\epsilon^2}{4}\right)^t.$$
lemmas.title: Auxiliary neighborhood moments

lemmas.proof_markdown:
For a fixed $L\in N_H(S)$, partition the $t$ seed lines by their intersection point with $L$. If $h_L<h$, there are at most $h-1$ parts. A part of size $r$ contains at least $r-1$ colliding seed pairs, so the partition contains at least $t-h+1$ colliding pairs.

A fixed pair of seed lines can collide on a target line only at the pair's own intersection. A parallel pair contributes no targets; a nonparallel pair has at most the $p+1$ affine lines through its intersection as targets. Double counting bad targets and colliding pairs gives

$$\left|\{L\in N_H(S):h_L<h\}\right|\le\frac{\binom t2(p+1)}{t-h+1}.$$

Since the fixed set $S$ has at least $M_t(H)$ common neighbors, subtraction proves all the displayed bounds for that same $S$.

If a polynomial explainer vanishes identically on every seed graph, the $h_L$ distinct intersections give $h_L$ distinct roots on the target graph. Thus the correction records the root supply relevant to interpolation.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P9, fix one $t$-line seed set $S$ supplied there, and write

$$N_H(S)=\bigcap_{M\in S}N_H(M).$$

For $L\in N_H(S)$, define

$$h_L=\left|\{L\cap M:M\in S\}\right|.$$

For this fixed $S$, every integer $h$ with $1\le h\le t$ satisfies

$$\left|\{L\in N_H(S):h_L\ge h\}\right|\ge M_t(H)-\frac{\binom t2(p+1)}{t-h+1}.$$
lemmas.title: Seed-intersection concurrency

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The KTZ coefficient-count construction gives

$$D_t=16(\lfloor\sqrt{dt}\rfloor+1)>16\sqrt{dt}.$$

Even before cleanup, transfer to a common-neighbor target requires $h_L>D_t$. Since $h_L\le t$, these inequalities imply

$$t>D_t>16\sqrt{dt},$$

and squaring gives the necessary condition $t>256d$. This condition is not asserted to be sufficient.

If the actual moment $M_t(H)$ is replaced by the guarantee obtainable from acceptance density alone in P9, then at the cubic scale this guarantee is

$$N_p\left(\frac{\epsilon_p^2}{4}\right)^t=p(p+1)\left(\frac{C^2d^{2/3}}{4p^{2/3}}\right)^t=O_{C,d,t}\left(p^{2-2t/3}\right),$$

which tends to $0$ for fixed $t>256d$. Thus, even before cleanup or concurrency subtraction, the density-only all-common-neighbor certificate is asymptotically vacuous and does not guarantee a target line in the lower-boundary asymptotic regime. This conclusion concerns only the density-derived guarantee, not the actual value of $M_t(H)$, and it does not rule out exploiting larger observed moments, label classes, or special structure in $H$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Fix an integer $d\ge101$, an integer $t\ge1$, and a constant $C>0$. Put

$$D_t=16(\lfloor\sqrt{dt}\rfloor+1).$$

Let $h_L$ be the number of distinct seed intersections on a common-neighbor target line for a $t$-line seed set, as in P10. If transfer requires $h_L>D_t$, then necessarily $t>256d$. For primes $p>d$, put

$$\epsilon_p=C\left(\frac dp\right)^{1/3},\qquad N_p=p(p+1).$$

For every fixed $d$, $t>256d$, and $C$,

$$N_p\left(\frac{\epsilon_p^2}{4}\right)^t=O_{C,d,t}\left(p^{2-2t/3}\right)\longrightarrow0$$

as $p\to\infty$ through primes.
lemmas.title: DRC parameter comparison

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Take the table constructed in P3. Entry P4 shows that its accepted carrier is connected; its degree description gives positive degree at every point and line, hence full support. Entry P5 gives equality in the point- and line-side distinct-star moment envelopes at every admissible order and gives the repeated line moment $\epsilon_0^r$. Entry P6 gives the displayed reaching bounds, whose scale is

$$\Theta\left(\frac{\theta p}{\epsilon_0}\right).$$

By P7, its raw accepted-incidence graph is also $K_{2,2}$-free. Nevertheless, the point table is $f=0$, so $Q=0$ is a legal polynomial of total degree at most $d$ and has global agreement $1$.

Thus connectivity, full support, moment extremality, and large reaching cost, separately or together, are not evidence against a perfect global decoder. A stronger soundness argument must use polynomial-label or value coherence. This is an incidence-only obstruction, not a claim that every auxiliary or label-aware dependent-random-choice argument fails.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and set $\epsilon_0=d/p$. There exists a valid affine line-versus-point table over $\mathbb F_p^2$ whose accepted carrier is connected and has positive degree at every affine point and line, which attains both distinct-star moment lower envelopes for every point-centered order $0\le s\le p+1$ and every line-centered order $0\le s\le p$, and whose line-centered with-replacement moment is $\epsilon_0^r$ for every integer $r\ge1$. For every $0<\theta\le1$, the same table satisfies

$$\frac{\theta p(p+1)}{d+1}\le\operatorname{OPT}_\theta\le\frac{\theta p(p+1)}{d-1}.$$

For this table, the polynomial $Q=0$ has total degree $0\le d$ and agrees with the point table at every point.
lemmas.title: Carrier scope

lemmas.proof_markdown:
KTZ Lemma 3.2 selects

$$|R|=O\left(\frac p\epsilon\right).$$

KTZ Lemma 2.2 and Lemmas 4.1--4.2 give a weighted-degree explainer with

$$D=O\left(\sqrt{d|R|}\right)=O\left(\sqrt{\frac{dp}{\epsilon}}\right).$$

Lemma 4.3 and the lifting step require this interpolation scale to fit the budget $D=O(\epsilon p)$. Thus one imposes

$$\sqrt{\frac{dp}{\epsilon}}=O(\epsilon p).$$

Squaring and rearranging gives

$$\epsilon^3=\Omega\left(\frac dp\right),$$

or equivalently the exponent-$1/3$ threshold up to constants. Under the stated KTZ trigger, Theorem 1.1 supplies one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with global agreement $\Omega(\epsilon)$. The selector's Chernoff, union-bound, and Chebyshev estimates cost constants but no power of $\epsilon$. This exponent calculation is a reconstruction of the benchmark chain, not a quoted KTZ theorem or an improved exponent.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $101\le d<p$, and let a valid affine line-versus-point table over $\mathbb F_p^2$ have point function $f$ and agreement $0<\epsilon\le1$. Suppose the KTZ selector has size $|R|=O(p/\epsilon)$, weighted interpolation uses degree $D=O(\sqrt{d|R|})$, and transfer and lifting require the resulting interpolation scale to fit the budget $D=O(\epsilon p)$. Then the interpolation scale is $D=O(\sqrt{dp/\epsilon})$, and compatibility of these scales requires

$$\epsilon^3=\Omega\left(\frac dp\right).$$

If additionally

$$\epsilon\ge C_{\mathrm{KTZ}}\left(\frac dp\right)^{1/3}$$

for the sufficiently large absolute constant in KTZ Theorem 1.1, then there is a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ and an absolute constant $c>0$ such that

$$\frac{|\{x\in\mathbb F_p^2:Q(x)=f(x)\}|}{p^2}\ge c\epsilon.$$
lemmas.title: KTZ parameter chain
